questions.question: Your team needs a single managed Azure workspace that lets data scientists train and deploy models with notebooks and the Python SDK, while business analysts use a no-code drag-and-drop designer. Which service fits best?
options: Azure AI Search (vector and keyword retrieval)
questions.explanation: Azure Machine Learning is the end-to-end managed ML platform on Azure. It provides Automated ML, the visual Designer, hosted notebooks, the Python/CLI v2 SDK, MLOps pipelines, managed endpoints and a model registry — covering both the SDK-driven and no-code personas in one workspace. Databricks is a Spark analytics platform without a built-in designer, Synapse is a unified analytics/data-warehouse service without notebook+designer ML tooling, and AI Search powers retrieval scenarios rather than model training.

questions.question: A developer wants to add vision, language, speech and decision features to an app by calling pre-built REST endpoints without training any model. Which family of Azure services should they use?
options: Azure HDInsight (managed Hadoop and Spark clusters)
questions.explanation: Azure AI services (the rebrand of Cognitive Services) is the family of pre-built, consumable AI APIs grouped into Vision, Language, Speech and Decision categories — exactly the surface a developer calls without training. Data Factory is for data movement, Logic Apps for workflow integration, and HDInsight for managed big-data clusters — none of them expose ready-to-call AI endpoints.

questions.question: Which type of machine learning is used to predict a continuous numeric value, such as the future selling price of a house from its features?
questions.explanation: Regression is a supervised learning technique that predicts a continuous numeric value (price, temperature, demand) by learning a function from labelled examples. Classification predicts a discrete category and would only return a price bucket, not a precise value; clustering groups unlabeled data into segments without ever producing a numeric prediction; and reinforcement learning learns a policy from environment rewards rather than fitting features to a target.

questions.question: An online retailer wants to automatically segment shoppers by purchase behaviour when no category labels are available. Which machine-learning approach is appropriate?
questions.explanation: Clustering is an unsupervised technique that groups items by feature similarity when no labels are provided; k-means and DBSCAN are common implementations. Classification and regression both need labelled training data, so they cannot run on an unlabeled shopper population, and anomaly detection looks for rare outliers rather than partitioning the entire population into segments.

questions.question: While preparing internal training on AI ethics, you must cite Microsoft's Responsible AI principles using Microsoft's exact published terminology. Which list uses the exact wording Microsoft publishes for its six Responsible AI principles?
options: Fairness; reliability and safety; confidentiality; inclusiveness; transparency; auditability
Fairness; reliability and safety; privacy and security; inclusiveness; transparency; accountability
Fairness; explainability; privacy and security; sustainability; transparency; human oversight
Reliability and safety; scalability; data minimisation; inclusiveness; interpretability; governance
questions.explanation: Microsoft's six Responsible AI principles are Fairness; Reliability and Safety; Privacy and Security; Inclusiveness; Transparency; and Accountability. The other lists substitute terms Microsoft does not use: 'explainability' or 'interpretability' for Transparency; 'human oversight', 'governance' or 'auditability' for Accountability; and unrelated terms (sustainability, scalability, data minimisation, confidentiality) that belong to other governance frameworks.

questions.question: Your application needs to detect human faces in images and analyse attributes such as head pose, with some features requiring an approved Limited Access application. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Face provides face detection, identification and attribute analysis. Several attributes (emotion, gender, age, makeup) are gated by the Limited Access programme and require an approved application. Vision Image Analysis covers general computer vision (tags, captions, OCR) but not identity matching, Document Intelligence extracts fields from forms, and Speech operates on audio rather than image data.

questions.question: Your finance team needs to pull structured fields, tables and key-value pairs out of invoices and receipts using both pre-built and custom-trained models. Which Azure service is designed for this?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Document Intelligence (formerly Form Recognizer) extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structured fields from documents using pre-built models (invoices, receipts, IDs, business cards) or models you train. Content Safety filters harmful text, Translator handles machine translation, and Personalizer is a decision service for content ranking — none of them parse document layouts.

questions.question: Which feature inside Azure AI Language scores the overall opinion in a passage of text as positive, neutral or negative with a confidence value?
questions.explanation: Sentiment analysis classifies a piece of text as positive, neutral or negative and returns a confidence score; the same feature also supports per-aspect opinion mining. Key phrase extraction surfaces the main concepts but does not judge tone, NER tags entities such as people, places and dates rather than scoring opinion, and language detection only identifies which language the text is written in.

questions.question: A call-centre app must transcribe live customer audio into text in real time. Which Azure AI Speech capability provides this?
questions.explanation: Speech to text converts spoken audio into written text using continuous recognition, either streamed in real time or from recorded files. Text to speech is the inverse (synthesising audio from a script), Speech translation converts spoken input across languages rather than producing same-language text, and Speaker recognition identifies or verifies a person by their voice without producing a transcript.

questions.question: Your team wants to build a chatbot that answers user questions from an existing collection of FAQs, product documents and support URLs. Which Azure capability is designed for that?
options: Azure AI Metrics Advisor (business KPI monitoring)
Azure AI Anomaly Detector (time-series outlier flagging)
Azure AI Bot Service (conversational hosting framework)
Azure AI Language question answering (knowledge-base QA)
questions.explanation: The question answering feature of Azure AI Language (the successor to QnA Maker) builds a knowledge base from documents, URLs and FAQs and serves natural-language answers. Bot Service is the conversational hosting layer that consumes such a knowledge base but does not build one from documents on its own, Metrics Advisor monitors KPI streams, and Anomaly Detector flags time-series outliers — neither indexes content for retrieval.

questions.question: A factory wants to flag unusual spikes in equipment-sensor time-series streams without training a model. Which Azure AI service should they use?
options: Azure AI Anomaly Detector (decision API for outliers)
Azure AI Content Safety (text and image moderation)
Azure AI Custom Vision (browser image classifier trainer)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Anomaly Detector is a pre-built decision service that finds anomalies in univariate or multivariate streams with little or no ML expertise. Translator converts text between languages, Custom Vision trains classifiers on labelled images, and Content Safety moderates harmful text and images — none of them analyse sensor data for unusual patterns.

questions.question: You want to train an image classifier from a small set of labelled photos using a web portal that requires no code. Which Azure AI service is purpose-built for this?
options: Azure AI Face (face detection and analysis)
Azure AI Vision (prebuilt Image Analysis API)
Azure AI Video Indexer (multimedia content insights)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Custom Vision (customvision.ai) lets you upload images, tag them, and train a custom image-classification or object-detection model through a browser portal, then export or call it via REST. Image Analysis only returns prebuilt tags and cannot be trained on your own classes, Video Indexer is for video streams rather than still images, and Face is dedicated to detecting and analysing human faces.

questions.question: Which Azure Machine Learning feature iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters to surface a high-quality model with minimal coding?
questions.explanation: Automated ML (AutoML) iterates through algorithms, featurisation and hyperparameters to produce a leaderboard of models for classification, regression, forecasting, NLP and computer-vision tasks. Hyperdrive tunes a single training script (one algorithm, parameter sweep only), MLflow simply logs runs and artefacts without choosing models, and the Designer is a drag-and-drop pipeline builder where the user still selects algorithms manually.

questions.question: When a team ships interpretability tooling that explains why a model produced a given prediction, which Microsoft Responsible AI principle is MOST directly supported?
questions.explanation: Transparency means people can understand how the AI system works and the basis of its decisions; interpretability tools such as SHAP and the Responsible AI dashboard in Azure ML support this principle. Fairness addresses biased outcomes across groups, Inclusiveness focuses on serving diverse users, and Reliability and Safety deals with consistent, safe operation — none of which is specifically about explaining individual predictions.

questions.question: An enterprise wants to use OpenAI GPT models inside Azure with regional hosting, private networking, content filters and Microsoft enterprise agreements. Which service should they choose?
questions.explanation: Azure OpenAI Service provides access to OpenAI's GPT, embeddings, DALL-E and Whisper models hosted on Azure with enterprise-grade security, regional availability, content filtering and integration with Azure networking and identity. Azure AI Language exposes prebuilt NLP features (sentiment, NER, translation, question answering) but does not surface GPT-family models; Azure AI Search is a retrieval and indexing service that often pairs with Azure OpenAI in RAG patterns but does not host the LLMs itself; and Bot Service is a conversational hosting framework that consumes language models rather than providing GPT.

questions.question: Which pattern grounds a generative AI model in current private knowledge by fetching relevant passages at inference time and passing them into the prompt, instead of changing the model weights?
questions.explanation: RAG retrieves the most relevant passages (often via vector search in Azure AI Search) and injects them into the prompt so the model answers using current, private content without altering its weights. Fine-tuning changes the weights themselves and requires retraining whenever the knowledge changes, RLHF aligns model behaviour through human preference data rather than supplying fresh facts, and prompt compression simply reduces token usage without adding any new knowledge.

questions.question: Which Azure AI service offers content filters that flag hate, violence, self-harm and sexual content in text and images, and is integrated with Azure OpenAI?
questions.explanation: Azure AI Content Safety analyses text and images for harmful categories (hate, violence, self-harm, sexual) with severity levels and also supports Prompt Shield and protected-material detection for generative AI scenarios. Personalizer ranks content for users but does not moderate it, Purview governs data lineage and classification at the enterprise level rather than runtime content filtering, and Translator only converts text between languages.

questions.question: Which Azure service is the natural choice to implement knowledge mining: indexing a large set of documents and enriching them with AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities) so users can search them?
options: Azure Data Lake Storage (raw file storage)
questions.explanation: Azure AI Search (formerly Cognitive Search) is the knowledge-mining service: it ingests documents from data sources, applies AI skills (OCR, key phrases, entities, vectors) and exposes a queryable Lucene-based index. It is also the typical retriever in RAG patterns. Data Lake stores raw files without indexing them, Cosmos DB is an operational NoSQL database rather than a search engine, and Document Intelligence extracts structured fields from individual forms but does not build a corpus-wide searchable index.

questions.question: A model scores very high on its training data but performs poorly on new, unseen samples. What is this behaviour called?
questions.explanation: Overfitting means the model has memorised the training data, including its noise, and fails to generalise to new examples. Mitigations include collecting more data, regularisation, simpler models, cross-validation and early stopping. Underfitting is the opposite (model too simple, scores poorly on both training and unseen data), class imbalance is about a skewed label distribution that biases predictions toward the majority class, and data drift is a change in input distribution after deployment — none of which describes high-training/low-test scores.

questions.question: On a strongly imbalanced binary-classification problem such as credit-card fraud detection, which metric gives the most informative view of model quality?
questions.explanation: F1-score (the harmonic mean of precision and recall) gives the most informative view on imbalanced classification because it penalises both missed positives and false alarms; precision/recall curves and AUC-PR are common companions. Plain accuracy is misleading — predicting only the majority class still yields a high score. MAE measures absolute error for regression targets, and R-squared measures explained variance in regression — neither applies to a discrete classification task.
